unit_title: Real Numbers and Irrational Numbers — 8.EE.2 correction block
purpose: Supply the independent mastery evidence for 8.EE.2 that release 1.0.0 does not contain. This assessment does not replace ma-g8-mathematics-u01-assessment; it is additional evidence covering only the corrected standard.

prompts.prompt: Write the exact solution or solutions of each equation using root notation: x² = 49, x² = 11, x³ = 27, x³ = 5. For each, state how many real solutions the equation has and why.

prompts.type: evaluation of perfect squares and cubes
prompts.prompt: Evaluate exactly, without a calculator: √121, √(16/49), ∛64, ∛(1/27). Verify two of your four answers using the inverse operation and show that verification.
For √45 and ∛50, state the two consecutive whole numbers each value lies between and explain how you know without a calculator. Then explain why neither can be written as an exact whole number.
Explain why √2 is irrational but √49 is rational. Give a reason rather than an assertion; reference the decimal expansion, the ratio-of-integers definition, or the informal contradiction argument.

A learner writes: “x² = 25, so x = 5,” and “∛(−27) has no real solution because you cannot take a root of a negative.” Identify what is wrong with each statement, correct it, and explain why the error is tempting.

A square garden bed must enclose 20 square feet. Give the exact side length in root notation, classify it as rational or irrational with a reason, give an approximation appropriate for buying lumber, and explain why the exact and rounded forms are each correct for their own purpose.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application, correct exact-versus-approximate discrimination, and a reasoned rather than asserted account of irrationality.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84%, or correct evaluation paired with inconsistent notation or explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check on a later occasion.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70%, or reliance on decimal approximations where exact values exist; reteach from the squaring-and-cubing inverse relationship using concrete area and volume models, then reassess on a separate occasion.

rubric_dimensions: Correct use of √ and ∛ notation to name exact solutions
Accuracy of evaluation for small perfect squares and perfect cubes
Discrimination between exact values and approximations, with justification
Quality of reasoning about rationality and irrationality
accommodation_guidance: Permit a squaring and cubing reference table for every learner; the target is root reasoning, not recall of the table.
Accept spoken, typed, handwritten, drawn, or manipulatives-based responses.
Allow extended time and a hidden timer; allow the assessment to be completed across two sittings.
Provide read-aloud support and reduced-copying formats; do not require the learner to transcribe the prompts.
The formal proof of the irrationality of √2 is never required for mastery at this grade.
mastery_rule: Do not mark 8.EE.2 mastered from this assessment alone. Require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
